newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse off earlier highs as offers creep in.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse off earlier highs as offers creep in.

text.p: Irish share prices slipped back from their earlier highs in morning trade on Thursday as some signs of profit-taking crept into the market, dealers said.
"The banks were marked up initially on the back of London but they are now off their highs and there are signs of offers creeping in," one dealer said.
By 1015 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was 23.05 points or 0.64 percent higher at 3600.00 after gaining nearly 50 points yesterday.

Dealers said the two main banks surged in early trading but later drifted back. Allied Irish Banks, which became the first Irish company to break the five billion punt capitalisation mark yesterday, touched 600 pence briefly before slipping back to 588, down two pence from the close.
Bank of Ireland edged up to 840 before settling at 830, a gain of 10 pence on the close, dealers said.
Irish Life, which yesterday announced that its joint bid with Kredietbank for a stake in Hungary's K&H Bank has been successful, gained 7.5 pence to 372.5.
Among industrial stocks, dealers reported good demand for CRH, which gained 10 pence to 685, and for Smurfit ahead of results from its U.S. associate Jefferson Smurfit Corporation later today.
Smurfit's share price was steady at 215.
